solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: 'formal' and 'binding' are eliminated quickly by 'No rule in the guild's charter', leaving a 2-way choice between tacit and fragile; 'fragile' is contradicted by 'for decades'
S030-01.notes: Never discussed (records never mention prices) yet consistently observed = unspoken, implicit agreement -> tacit. Formal/binding contradict 'no rule'; fragile contradicts decades-long stability.

flags: minor: 'belied' is a low-frequency word many students won't know, but the contrast (barely two centimeters vs. never-before-observed pattern) is clear enough that elimination of 'reflected' and 'determined' works
S030-02.notes: Small size vs. large significance = size gave a false impression of significance -> belied. Reflected/determined imply size matched or caused significance; exaggerated is backward.

flags: minor: A is a true detail from sentence 1 (detail-vs-main-idea trap) but weak; B and C are unsupported and few would pick them
S030-03.notes: Text centers on the multigenerational migration: no individual completes the return; descendants do. Factually accurate (eastern monarch migration, super generation flies south).

S030-04.notes: Plentiful/easy food yields worse condition because it's low in protein -> content matters more than ease of access. A contradicts passage; C is speculative; D reverses (low protein, not too much). Edmonton study (Murray et al. 2015) found human-food diets linked to poorer condition and mange — consistent.

S030-05.notes: Percent reductions: dot 14/20=70%, UV 18/40=45%, netting 6/10=60%. D gives all three correctly and shows dot film is greatest relative to starting level. A uses absolute drop (favors UV); B favors netting; C compares absolute final counts across groups with different baselines. All numbers in choices are arithmetically correct.

flags: minor: D is a clear misreading few would pick; A contradicts Text 2 outright
S030-06.notes: Text 2: human-raised wolves succeed, shelter dogs struggle -> experience matters more than recognized -> Text 1 overlooks developmental contact. B goes beyond Text 2 (chimps not discussed). Consistent with Udell et al. findings.

flags: minor: B copies one note verbatim and states the result but omits the expectation that makes it surprising — reasonable trap
S030-07.notes: Surprise requires contrast of expectation (more receptors) with result (poorer discrimination). 12/3 = 4 times, correct. 'Worse' is a fair synthesis of 'could not reliably distinguish colors people easily tell apart'. C gives only expectation; D gives explanation. Consistent with Thoen et al. 2014 (Science).

S030-08.notes: Benefit (kelp recovery) followed by a downside (conflict with shellfish harvesters) -> concession/contrast 'Even so'. Similarly, As a result (conflict not caused by kelp regrowth), In other words don't fit.

S030-09.notes: Appositive 'a fifteenth-century book written in an unknown script' opens with a comma after 'manuscript', so must close with a comma before 'has resisted'. A leaves appositive unclosed; dash mismatches comma; semicolon separates subject from verb.

S030-10.notes: Clause after 'noticed that' needs a finite verb; killing occurred before the noticing -> past perfect 'had killed'. 'has killed' is wrong tense in past narrative; 'killing'/'to kill' leave the clause without a finite verb. Fleming facts (Sept 1928, return from vacation, contaminated plate) accurate.

S030-11.notes: Sentence 2 reports the instrument-measured Draupner wave, which challenged models predicting such waves were extremely rare. A wrongly calls it exaggerated; B assigns the revision to sentence 2 (it's sentence 3); C misreads 'more common than believed' as 'more common today'. Draupner wave ~25.6 m with significant wave height ~12 m, Jan 1 1995 — accurate.
